analysis:
The PR is docs-only: docs/architecture/inference.md gets a date bump (line 3) and a new paragraph at head lines 1960-1973 (after the base text around line 1958). The paragraph says JSON response_format (json_object or json_schema) on the Qwen template family defaults to a closed thinking block unless the caller overrides it with reasoning.enabled, enable_thinking, chat_template_kwargs, a reasoning effort, or a positive reasoning.max_tokens. It also says the coordinator prompt sidecar mirrors the rule so cache planning renders the same prompt. No code or control change is visible in the supplied evidence.

Security relevance: the described behavior changes how the prompt template is rendered, which affects the prompt-contract identity used in cache-salt derivation (T-041 and the coordinator cache_route_keys path). The documented mirroring in the sidecar is what keeps exact-routing and prefix-cache planning consistent. A provider/sidecar divergence would be a cache-correctness or availability matter, not a confidentiality regression. Cross-account isolation is unchanged: the salt is coordinator-authored from authenticated account, model build, prompt contract and block-hash version, and the claim here is only that the contract ID reflects the rendered prompt. The sampler and thinking default are not part of cache identity, as the base text states.

The doc also says Qwen4SupportPolicy.validateReasoningContext accepts the closed block, so no new 400 or 500 trigger is described. I found no new attack surface, no weakened mitigation and no invalidated assumption. The remaining unverified item is that the code actually matches the documented behavior, in particular the coordinator sidecar mirroring and the public prompt vectors. Those implementations are outside the supplied batch and not verifiable here, so a code-level pass over Qwen35TemplateFix and the sidecar would be needed to confirm the parity.
